nodes.summary: A single cross term `E[X_j · X_i · 1_{T > i}]` (with `j < i`) vanishes when the `X_i` are identically distributed with zero mean and `X_i` is independent of `(X_j, 1_{T > i})`.
nodes.title: Vanishing of a single cross term in Wald's second equation

nodes.summary: Square-integrability of the maximal stopped partial sum, in v1's form: `max_{0 ≤ k ≤ T} Sₖ²` is integrable. This is v1's `integrable_maximal_stopped_partial_sum_sq`, whose proof in v1 was left unproved.
nodes.title: Square-integrability of the maximal stopped partial sum

nodes.summary: Square-integrability of a stopped partial sum, general-filtration form.
nodes.title: Square-integrability of a stopped partial sum

nodes.summary: The stopped sum of squares is integrable under the stated diagonal hypotheses.
nodes.title: Integrability of the stopped sum of squares

nodes.summary: A successor step adds exactly the next observation to the predictable filtration.
nodes.title: Successor step of the predictable filtration

nodes.summary: The predictable filtration contains no observations at time zero.
nodes.title: Predictable filtration at time zero is trivial

nodes.summary: The "predictable" filtration associated to a sequence `X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ`: `ℱ_k = σ(X_0, …, X_{k-1})`. Ported verbatim from v1 `WaldSecondEquation.lean`.
nodes.title: Predictable filtration of a sequence

nodes.summary: Algebraic identity expanding the square of a finite sum into diagonal and cross-term contributions: `(∑_{i<n} f i)^2 = ∑_{i<n} (f i)^2 + 2 ∑_{i<n} ∑_{j<i} f j · f i`.
nodes.title: Square of a finite sum as diagonal plus cross terms

nodes.summary: The total cross-term contribution vanishes for a stopping time bounded by a constant, with no extra summability or measurability hypotheses: the sums are finite, and every term past the bound is zero.
nodes.title: Cross terms vanish for a bounded stopping time

nodes.summary: The full cross-term contribution to `E[(S_T)^2]` vanishes: `E[∑_{i < T} ∑_{j < i} X_j X_i] = 0` for identically distributed, mean-zero variables, with each `X_i` independent of the filtration at time `i` and measurable at time `i + 1`, given absolute summability of the stopped cross-term series.
nodes.title: Vanishing of the cross terms in Wald's second equation

nodes.summary: Wald's equation applied to the squared increments gives the diagonal identity.
nodes.title: Diagonal identity in Wald's second equation

nodes.summary: Let `Xᵢ` be identically distributed integrable real random variables and `T` a stopping time with `E T < ∞`, with each `Xₖ` independent of the filtration at time `k`. Then `E[S_T] = E[X₁] · E[T]`, where `S_T = ∑_{i < T} Xᵢ`.
nodes.title: Wald's equation

nodes.summary: Under Wald's hypotheses, the stopped sum is integrable. This reuses Wald's summable `L¹` series and applies Mathlib's sum measurability and norm bound.
nodes.title: Integrability of the stopped sum in Wald's equation

nodes.summary: Let $(\Omega, \mathbb{P})$ be a probability space with a filtration $(\mathcal{F}_k)_{k \ge 0}$, and let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be identically distributed real random variables with $\mathbb{E}|X_0| < \infty$, $\mathbb{E}[X_0] = 0$ and $\mathbb{E}[X_0^2] < \infty$. Let $T$ be an $\mathbb{N}$-valued stopping time for $(\mathcal{F}_k)$ with $\mathbb{E}[T] < \infty$. Suppose each $X_k$ is independent of $\mathcal{F}_k$ and…
nodes.title: Wald's second equation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
